Border final class

The 13 corner / edge / interior runes that make up a rectangular box border. Outer runes drive Style boxes; the five middle-* runes drive Table separators (column splits, row separators, cross intersections).

static markdownBorder(): selfGitHub-flavored Markdown table border. Mirrors lipgloss's Border::markdownBorder() — pipes for the verticals, dashes for the horizontals, plain | corners. Useful when an already-rendered Table\Table grid (this lib's own Markdown-capable table) needs to round-trip through a Markdown reader without losing its grid.

Mirrors btop Draw::createBox (title / title2 args) and Draw::update_clock (btop_draw.cpp, Symbols title_left ┐ / title_right ┌, title_left_down ┘ / title_right_down └).
embedJunctions(bool $bottom = false): arrayThe default [open, close] junction pair for an embedded title on the top ($bottom = false) or bottom edge. Taken from the border's own opposite corners so every family stays consistent — ┐┌/┘└ for normal and rounded, ┓┏/┛┗ thick, ╗╔/╝╚ double, ++ ascii — with the rounded arcs squared off, matching btop which always embeds with square junctions even on rounded boxes.
seam(bool $left, bool $right, bool $up, bool $down): stringThe rune for a point where lines leave in the given directions — the junction a seam (an internal divider) makes where it meets a frame or another seam. btop's divider law (Symbols div_left ├, div_right ┤, div_up ┬, div_down ┴): a vertical seam landing on the top edge is seam(left: true, right: true, down: true) → ┬.

titles(): arrayAttached titles, keyed by TitleAnchor case name, each anchor's list in insertion order.

Layout final class

Compositional layout primitives.

MethodSummary
static width(string $block): intCell width of $block. For multi-line blocks it's the widest line.
static height(string $block): intNumber of lines in $block.
static size(string $block): arrayWidth / height pair. Useful for checking that a child fits inside a fixed-size container before placing.
static joinHorizontal(float $pos, string ...$blocks): stringStitch blocks side by side. $pos is a vertical anchor (Top/ Center/Bottom or any 0.0-1.0 float): shorter blocks are padded vertically with blank lines anchored per $pos. Per-line widths are equalised with trailing spaces so the output is rectangular.
static joinHorizontalWithSpacing(float $pos, ?int $spacing, string ...$blocks): stringStitch blocks side by side with explicit spacing.
static joinVertical(float $pos, string ...$blocks): stringStack blocks top-to-bottom. $pos is a horizontal anchor (Left/Center/Right or any 0.0-1.0 float): narrower blocks get padded horizontally with spaces anchored per $pos.
static joinVerticalWithSpacing(float $pos, ?int $spacing, string ...$blocks): stringStack blocks top-to-bottom with explicit spacing.
static joinHorizontalWithDivider(float $pos, string $divider, string ...$blocks): stringStitch blocks side by side with a divider column between each adjacent pair. Empty blocks ('', zero width) are dropped together with their divider, so a collapsed pane leaves no orphan rule. A single-line $divider is repeated on every row; a multi-line one is laid out row by row (missing rows blank). An empty $divider degrades to joinHorizontal().
static joinVerticalWithDivider(float $pos, string $divider, string ...$blocks): stringStack blocks top-to-bottom with a rule line between each adjacent pair, the rule tiled (repeated, then cut on a cell boundary) to the widest block. Empty blocks are dropped together with their rule. An empty $divider degrades to joinVertical().
static tile(string $unit, int $width): stringRepeat $unit until it covers $width cells, then cut to exactly that.
static clipHead(string $block, int $rows): stringKeep at most $rows lines from the top of $block.
static clipTail(string $block, int $rows): stringKeep at most $rows lines from the bottom of $block.
static clipWidth(string $block, int $cols, string $ellipsis = ''): stringKeep at most $cols visible cells of every line. The cut is ANSI-aware (escapes carry no width, a trailing reset survives) and lands on a grapheme boundary. With $ellipsis set an overlong line keeps $cols - width(ellipsis) cells and gains the ellipsis.
static place(int $width, int $height, float $hPos, float $vPos, string $block, string $fill = ' '): stringPosition $block within a $width × $height rectangle. $hPos and $vPos are 0.0-1.0 anchors (use the Position constants). The fill character defaults to a space; passing a styled blank (e.g. Style::new()->background(...)->render(' ')) lets the surrounding area carry a colour.
static placeHorizontal(int $width, float $pos, string $block, string $fill = ' '): stringPosition horizontally only — pads each line in $block to $width with $fill, anchored per $pos. No vertical change.
static placeVertical(int $height, float $pos, string $block, string $fill = ' '): stringPosition vertically only — pads $block above/below to reach $height rows, anchored per $pos. Each blank row is width($block) cells wide.

Output final class

Top-level (un-styled) output helpers — the equivalents of the package-level lipgloss.Print / Println / Sprint / Fprint / Printf functions. Each method is the un-styled twin of the matching Style method (Output::sprint() vs Style::sprint(), and so on) so callers can reach the same shape without a Style instance.

MethodSummary
static sprint(string ...$parts): stringConcatenate arguments with single spaces. No newline, no styling. Un-styled twin of Style::sprint() (same join rule and same Go divergence, both documented in the class docblock).
static printf(string $format, mixed ...$args): stringsprintf() substitution that RETURNS the formatted string (upstream Printf writes instead). Un-styled twin of Style::printfSprint().
static print(string ...$parts): intWrite Output::sprint($parts) to STDOUT (no newline). Un-styled twin of Style::print(). Same fail-fast write accounting: returns the bytes written, throws RuntimeException on an invalid STDOUT or a false/short write.
static println(string ...$parts): intWrite Output::sprint($parts) . "\n" to STDOUT. Un-styled twin of Style::println(). Same fail-fast write accounting as print().
static fprint($stream, string ...$parts): intWrite Output::sprint($parts) to a caller-supplied stream resource (no trailing newline). Un-styled twin of Style::fprint().

Renderer final class

Per-writer rendering context. Mirrors lipgloss's Renderer — a small value object that bundles a ColorProfile and a "dark background" flag so callers can branch on those without threading them through every Style construction.

MethodSummary
static new(): selfDefault renderer: TrueColor profile, dark background. Convenience for the common case (most modern terminals).
static fromEnvironment(): selfAuto-detect the color profile from the environment via ColorProfile::detectTerminal(), memoised per process and per distinct environment fingerprint (self::$environmentMemo). The dumb-terminal veto matters here: TERM=dumb answers NoTty, so no SGR reaches a terminal that cannot honour it, as before P1-10a. The dark-background flag stays at its default (true) since that's not detectable without an OSC 11 round trip — toggle it explicitly via withHasDarkBackground() once the program has the answer.
static resetEnvironmentMemoForTesting(): voidDrop every memoised environment detection. Same seam shape as \SugarCraft\Style\Layout\SolverFactory::resetEnvironmentResolutionForTesting(), separate statics — tests that flip colour variables call this to start from a cold memo.
withColorProfile(ColorProfile $p): selfOverride the color profile (downsamples colours when rendering).
withHasDarkBackground(bool $isDark): selfOverride the dark-background flag. Bubble Tea programs set this from a BackgroundColorMsg::isDark() reply on startup; for non-interactive output, leave at the default.
newStyle(): StyleCreate a fresh Style pre-configured with this renderer's color profile. Equivalent to Style::new()->colorProfile($p).
lightDark(): \ClosureBind this renderer's hasDarkBackground to a LightDark picker. Equivalent to LightDark::picker($r->hasDarkBackground).
resolveAdaptive(AdaptiveColor $color): \SugarCraft\Core\Util\ColorResolve an AdaptiveColor with this renderer's dark-bg flag. Mirrors lipgloss Renderer.HasDarkBackground + adaptive pick.

Style final class

Immutable styled-text builder. Each setter returns a new Style.

MethodSummary
static setDefaultProfile(?ColorProfile $profile): voidPin the ambient profile for styles created by new() from now on; null restores TrueColor.
static defaultProfile(): ?ColorProfileThe ambient profile currently in force, or null when none was negotiated.
static getDefaultProfile(): ?ColorProfilePrefix-spelled alias of self::defaultProfile() from the lipgloss-era naming; the bare slot never collided (the static property and a method name are separate namespaces).
static withDefaultProfile(?ColorProfile $profile, callable $callable): mixedScoped gate over the ambient default profile: pins $profile for the duration of $callable, then restores whatever was in force — finally-guarded, so an exception thrown inside still unwinds cleanly. Collapses the per-callsite save/restore ritual (finding 020) into one call; nesting is safe (each gate reinstalls its own predecessor) and null behaves as in setDefaultProfile() (TrueColor minting inside the block).
static new(): self
setString(string $content): selfBind a default content string to the style. Calling render() with no argument then renders this string. Mirrors lipgloss's SetString().
value(): ?stringBound default content (set via setString() / of()), or null.
underlineColor(Color|string|null $c): selfColoured underline, separate from the foreground colour. Mirrors lipgloss's UnderlineColor. Emits SGR 58;... (xterm-256 extension) when underlining is active. Accepts the same input shape as fg() — a Color, a 3- or 6-digit hex string, or null to clear; a bad string refuses with the shared InvalidArgumentException path, not a TypeError. Tier caveat: SGR 58 has no 4-bit form, so at the Ansi profile the colour falls back to the FOREGROUND slot and recolours the glyphs themselves (Color::toUnderline()), rather than tinting the line.
getUnderlineColor(): ?ColorUnderline color (SGR 58), or null when default.
underlineStyle(UnderlineStyle $style): selfUnderline-line shape (single / double / curly / dotted / dashed), emitted as the SGR 4:N sub-parameter. A non-None shape also switches underline() on (an explicit later underline(false) still wins; None leaves the flag alone), so the shape never silently renders nothing. The wire form is unchanged (ruled): only 4:N, no plain SGR 4 companion. Terminals that understand SGR 4:N render the styled underline; terminals that don't typically ignore the extended form and render no underline at all, since no plain SGR 4 companion is emitted. Mirrors lipgloss UnderlineStyle.
getUnderlineStyle(): UnderlineStyleUnderline shape (single / double / curly / dotted / dashed / none).
paddingChar(string $char): selfGlyph used to fill padding cells. Default ' '. Single-cell graphemes are recommended; wider clusters render but break lipgloss-style width math. Mirrors lipgloss PaddingChar.
getPaddingChar(): stringGlyph used to fill padding cells (default ' ').
marginChar(string $char): selfGlyph used to fill margin cells. Default ' '. Mirrors lipgloss MarginChar.
getMarginChar(): stringGlyph used to fill margin cells (default ' ').
foreground(?Color $c): selfSet the foreground color. Pass null to clear (no SGR emitted).
background(?Color $c): selfSet the background color. Pass null to clear.
fg(Color|string|null $c): selfShort alias for foreground(). Accepts a Color, hex string (e.g. '#ff5'), or null to clear.
bg(Color|string|null $c): selfShort alias for background(). Same input shape as fg().
on(Color|string|null $c): selfReads naturally in chains: $s->fg('#ffffff')->on('#0000ff'). Same as bg() (hex string, Color or null) but English-shaped.
of(string $content): selfShort alias for setString() — bind a default content string. After ->of('hello'), render() with no argument uses that string.
foregroundAdaptive(Color|string $light, Color|string $dark): selfStore a foreground pair for resolveAdaptive() to collapse: $light for terminals with a light background, $dark for terminals with a dark one. render() never consults the pair — the light-vs-dark answer is ambient knowledge the style does not have — and rendering with the pair still uncollapsed throws a LogicException. Until the ritual runs, an explicit foreground slot wins.
backgroundAdaptive(Color|string $light, Color|string $dark): self
foregroundComplete(Color|string $trueColor, Color|string $ansi256, Color|string $ansi): selfStore a foreground that picks per-tier from the supplied triple based on the live ColorProfile. render() collapses the triple itself (the tier lives on the style, so nothing ambient is needed); resolveProfile() materialises the same pick into the concrete slot. Use this when you want to override the automatic downsampling with designer-chosen values for each terminal capability tier. Mirrors lipgloss v2's CompleteColor; assign a pre-built triple through withCompleteForeground() instead (named arguments there keep the tier semantics attached to each value, which is what makes positional misorder invisible).
backgroundComplete(Color|string $trueColor, Color|string $ansi256, Color|string $ansi): self
withAdaptiveForeground(AdaptiveColor $pair): selfFeed a pre-built AdaptiveColor pair into the adaptive foreground slot — the value-object twin of foregroundAdaptive(), byte-identical downstream (same slot, same set-flags). Upstream lipgloss assigns the pair (its lightdark.Color struct) directly to the style field; this restores that shape after the flattened positional port. The same fail-fast contract applies: render() refuses while the pair is uncollapsed.
withAdaptiveBackground(AdaptiveColor $pair): selfValue-object twin of backgroundAdaptive().
withCompleteForeground(CompleteColor $triple): selfFeed a pre-built CompleteColor triple into the complete foreground slot — the value-object twin of foregroundComplete(), byte-identical downstream. Construct with named arguments to keep each tier bound to its value.
withCompleteBackground(CompleteColor $triple): selfValue-object twin of backgroundComplete().
resolveAdaptive(bool $isDark): selfCollapse any adaptive fg/bg slots into concrete foreground / background based on the supplied dark-background flag (typically the value of \SugarCraft\Core\Msg\BackgroundColorMsg::isDark()).
resolveProfile(): selfCollapse any complete-colour fg/bg slots into concrete foreground / background based on the style's current colour profile. Explicit concrete colours win, matching lipgloss precedence. render() collapses complete slots on its own, so this is only needed to materialise (or re-materialise after a colorProfile() change) the pick for inspection — the adaptive axis has no automatic path and must come through resolveAdaptive().

maxWidth(?int $w): selfCap rendered width to $w cells (truncate longer lines). Unlike width(), doesn't pad shorter content. Mirrors lipgloss's MaxWidth. Pass null to remove the cap.

inline(bool $on = true): selfForce the rendered output onto a single line. Newlines in content are replaced with spaces; padding-top/bottom and margin-top/bottom collapse to zero. Mirrors lipgloss's Inline().
wordWrap(bool $on = true): selfWord-wrap content to width() instead of truncating it. Opt-in: the default keeps width()'s truncation, which existing consumers and the README rely on. Breaks fall on whitespace where the line allows, a word wider than the budget is broken across lines, and SGR styling carries across each break (Width::wrapAnsi()). Without a width() this is a no-op: there is no budget to wrap to. Under inline() it is also a no-op: inline() promises one line, so width() truncation applies instead.
marginBackground(?Color $c): selfSet the colour painted into the margin area (outside the border). Defaults to no colour; useful for full-width status bars.

Tabular data renderer. Builds a string with column-aligned cells, an optional header row, and an optional border (using the middle-* runes from Border).

MethodSummary
static new(): self
headers(string ...$headers): self
row(string ...$cells): self
rows(iterable $rows): self
clearRows(): selfDrop every body row but keep the headers + every other setting intact. Mirrors lipgloss's ClearRows(). Useful when you want to refill a static-headers table from a streaming data source.
data(Data $data): selfBulk-replace body rows from any Data source. Mirrors lipgloss's Data(StringData) setter — pass StringData (or any custom Data implementation) for streaming ingest.
border(?Border $b): self
headerAlign(Align $a): self
rowAlign(Align $a): self
styleFunc(?\Closure $fn): selfPer-cell style callback. $fn($row, $col) is called for every data cell (including the header — row index === Table::HEADER_ROW for the header). Return a Style; the cell content is wrapped in Style::render() before alignment / border join.
borderTop(bool $on = true): selfToggle borders per side. Each is on by default. Mirrors lipgloss's Border() / BorderTop() / BorderRight() / ….
borderRight(bool $on = true): self
borderBottom(bool $on = true): self
borderLeft(bool $on = true): self
borderHeader(bool $on = true): selfToggle the header / body separator row. Default on.
borderRow(bool $on = true): selfDraw a separator row between every body row. Default off.
borderColumn(bool $on = true): selfDraw vertical separators between columns. Default on. Off → cells join with a single space separator.
width(?int $cells): selfCap the rendered table width to $cells columns. When set, columns are shrunk proportionally (lipgloss-style) to fit within the cap, with a minimum of 1 cell content per column. Cell content that still exceeds the shrunken column width is truncated via Width::truncateAnsi (unless a wrap() callback is set, which then receives the shrunken width and may spread the cell over several lines). The cap is best-effort: border runes, the one-space cell padding and the 1-cell column floor are never shrunk, so a cap smaller than that fixed overhead (e.g. on all-empty rows) renders wider than requested. Pass null to remove the cap.
offset(int $n): selfSkip the first $n body rows when rendering (after header). Useful for pagination. Default 0.
wrap(?\Closure $fn): selfCell-overflow wrap callback. Receives the raw cell value and the column's content width (after any width() cap shrink) and returns the cell's lines. When set, the callback is invoked per-cell in place of the default Width::truncateAnsi truncation, and EVERY returned line is rendered: a row whose cells wrap to N lines occupies N physical lines, shorter cells padded with blank lines. A returned line still wider than the column is truncated with Width::truncateAnsi so the grid never misaligns; an empty list renders as one blank line.
render(): string

Connector character set used by Tree. Each preset bundles four runes: branch (intermediate child), lastBranch (terminal child), indent (continuation prefix for an intermediate ancestor), and lastIndent (continuation prefix when the ancestor was the last child).
